row.name: East Ridge via Dykeman Pass
row.description: Take the Blue Canyon Trail to its north end, continue up to Dykeman Pass, drop into the Alpine Creek drainage and climb talus to the east ridge. The ridge has some class 3 scrambling.

row.name: Temple, Galey, Sill Traverse
row.overview: Stamina and navigation are tested by this ridge link of Temple Crag, Galey and Sill, around 1.8 miles long. Routes on Temple Crag start at 5.7 and top out at 5.10c. Galey is much chossier than Temple and Sill, with nothing over 5.7, and gets better nearer the top. From Galey, a ridge of class 2-3 drops to Glacier Notch; crossing the L-shaped couloir leads to Sill's Swiss Arete. Extending to Thunderbolt is possible; the quickest way back to Palisade Glacier is Underhill Couloir (class 4, loose).
row.approach: Start at the Glacier Lodge trailhead at the end of Crocker Street west of Big Pine, and follow the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail past First Lake. There are two main places to cross the creek: on the east shore of Second Lake (reached between First and Second Lakes) and at the Third Lake outlet. The first is more reliable when water is high. The spots to leave the main trail are well used. After crossing, walk off-trail up to the foot of Temple Crag.
row.descent_text: The traverse ends on Mount Sill. From its summit, descend the third-class ridge in the direction of Polemonium, then drop into the L-shaped couloir and Glacier Notch to reach the Palisade Glacier. The starts of both are not obvious, but cairns usually mark them. From the glacier, you can either go straight down to Second or Third Lake, which is more direct and best with snow, or follow the trail past Sam Mack Meadow to rejoin the North Fork of Big Pine Creek trail.

row.name: South West Ridge (aka Yellow Brick Road)
Austrian Arete
row.overview: Follows the arete bordering the wide southeast side of Thunderbolt Peak, a face marked by a big white dike slanting across it. The arete is hard to make out until you are on the face. The 5th class rock ranges from good to excellent for the most part. At one spot the arete narrows and is crossed by straddling it and shimmying upward, which is exposed. Past this stretch, a lost arrow is fixed at the foot of a small step as protection. One to two pitches short of the summit area the arete flattens (4th class and some snow).

row.name: Silver Linings Arete
row.overview: A bolted arete line that merges with the West Arete for its last 1100 ft or so; the rock is surprisingly good. The walk in from South Lake takes 3-5 hours over Bishop Pass, traversing beneath Agassiz and losing a little height rather than sidehilling talus. P1 5.10a (170'), P2 5.9 (120'), P3 5.9 (120', bolt), P4 5.10c (120'; the follower needs protecting on the leftward traverse), P5 5.10b (180', 2 bolts), P6 5.10c (180', 1 bolt) to a huge ledge, then the knife-edge. Descend the east arete and the south chute, left at the fork, with one rappel.
row.approach: From South Lake, follow the Bishop Pass trail over the pass, then contour beneath Mt. Agassiz toward Mt. Winchell, staying at roughly the same elevation. Dropping slightly is easier than sidehilling the talus. Camping is possible at Dusy Basin or at the lakes by Isosceles Peak. The route starts to the right of the initial scrambling of the West Arete, and it joins the West Arete near the knife-edge section.
row.descent_text: From the summit, descend the east arete (third class), dropping to the second chute on that side and following it down, then traverse to Winchell Col without losing elevation. West of the col, take the left of the two forks and downclimb a loose gully at third to fourth class. A rappel station on the left side of the gully serves the drop-off partway down, and easier ground lies below it. The chutes on the west face are poor ways down.

row.name: Goode Earth
row.overview: A line of clean dihedrals on a subsidiary buttress of the north face. Thin cracks dominate; protection is awkward in spots but always available, and the crux is short. Alpine hazards include loose blocks and ledges covered in scree. P1 (5.9, 100'): fingercrack, then the dihedral left. P2 (5.10a, 150'): the Green Dihedral. P3 (5.10a, 140'): steep fingercrack crux, then a poorly protected 5.7 R slab; belay right, not on the larger left ledge. P4 (5.9, 110'): the Yellow Jamcrack. P5 (5.7+, 140'): crescent ramp. P6 (4th class, 150'): to the top. For the summit, scramble the 2nd class east ridge. The walk-off goes down 2nd class slopes to the southeast, joining the trail over Bishop Pass.
row.approach: Use the standard North Buttress approach from the South Lake trailhead along the Bishop Pass trail. The route is on the buttress just east of the North Buttress, and the start is reached by scrambling over snow, talus and third class ledges.
row.descent_text: The buttress tops out on the ridge below the summit. A second-class scramble along the east ridge reaches the summit if wanted. Descend the southeast slopes, second class, back to the Bishop Pass trail near Saddlerock Lake.

row.name: Inconsolable Traverse
row.overview: Ridge traverse across the Inconsolable Range, running between Cloudripper and Mount Agassiz. Leave the lot at South Lake, walk up beside the pipeline for water, an old one, toward Brown Lake, and at the foot of that lake's valley turn right (S) onto an open ridge that climbs to the top of Cloudripper. Partway up, an unseen notch has to be downclimbed (fourth class to easy fifth). Past the summit the crest turns jagged, passing Picture Puzzle before Mount Agassiz. Hardness varies with proximity to the crest; 5.5/5.6 at most, often a bit loose.
